words.tip: 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo) = “Are you at peace?” (안녕 annyeong = peace).

topics.name: Numbers

words.tip: Two number systems: 일 (il) for dates & money, 하나 (hana) for counting things & age.

topics.note: Left: Sino-Korean numbers (dates, money). Right: native Korean numbers (counting things, age).

words.tip: 물 (mul) ≈ “mool”, like a pool of water.
밥 (bap) means cooked rice AND “a meal”: 밥 먹었어요? (bap meogeosseoyo?) = “Did you eat?” (a common greeting).
Girls say 오빠 (oppa), boys say 형 (hyeong).
Girls say 언니 (eonni), boys say 누나 (nuna).
네 (ne) means YES, even though it sounds like “nay”!

sentences.en: I have a lot of homework today.
Do you want to watch a movie?
I'm going to see a doctor.
Dad is cooking in the kitchen.
I clean my room on Sundays.
I take the subway to school.
What do you do for work?
I have a meeting at ten.
I want to be a chef.
Let's go to the park together.

topics.name: Grammar: Past tense

sentences.en: I went to the park yesterday.
I saw a movie last week.

topics.note: Past: add 았/었 (at/eot) + 어요 (eoyo): 가요 (gayo) → 갔어요 (gasseoyo), 먹어요 (meogeoyo) → 먹었어요 (meogeosseoyo), 해요 (haeyo) → 했어요 (haesseoyo).

topics.name: Grammar: Future

sentences.en: I will go to the beach tomorrow.
Next year I will travel a lot.
My dream is to be a singer.

topics.note: Future/intention: ～(으)ㄹ 거예요 ((eu)l geoyeyo): 가다 (gada) → 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo). A promise to someone: ～(으)ㄹ게요 ((eu)lgeyo): 전화할게요 (jeonhwahalgeyo).

topics.name: Grammar: Questions
topics.note: Same ending as a statement, just raise your voice at the end: 맞아요? (majayo?). Question words: 뭐 (mwo), 누구 (nugu), 어디 (eodi), 언제 (eonje), 왜 (wae).

topics.name: Grammar: Negation
topics.note: Put 안 (an) before the verb = don't: 안 먹어요 (an meogeoyo). 못 (mot) = can't: 못 해요 (mot haeyo). 없어요 (eopseoyo) = don't have / there isn't.

topics.name: Grammar: Polite vs casual

sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom? (polite)

topics.note: ～요 (yo) endings are polite (해요 haeyo); dropping 요 is casual 반말 (banmal) for close friends: 고마워요 (gomawoyo) → 고마워 (gomawo). ～ㅂ니다 (mnida) is extra formal.
